newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African arms deal clears cabinet hurdle.
newsitem.headline: S.African arms deal clears cabinet hurdle.

text.p: South Africa's cabinet on Wednesday approved a key report on the country's defence needs, clearing one of the last hurdles to the purchase of four corvettes and several submarines.
"The cabinet...approved policy proposals contained in the defence review concerning defence posture, functions (and) force design," a statement from President Nelson Mandela's office said.
Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils, among those who believes the South African navy needs more ships, told Reuters the cabinet decision was "a significant vote of confidence for defence".

"It sends the right signals to the South African National Defence Force and to the defence industry," he said. "The decision supports the core force option and opens the way for deciding what is militarily, fiscally and industrially viable."
The "core force option" in the defence review envisages, among other things, the navy being equipped with four corvettes and four submarines.
The navy currently has no corvettes.
It has four submarines, but they are obsolete.

The finance ministry's 1997/98 budget for defence makes no provision for major arms acquisitions, but Kasrils and Defence Minister Joe Modise have said approval of the defence review would open the way to funds being found for corvettes and submarines.
Modise has said several countries, including Britain, have put forward counter-trade proposals under which South Africa could obtain navy vessels on very good terms.

The defence review approved by cabinet on Wednesday still has to win parliamentary approval. But the review, conducted over more than a year, already has the blessing of influential parliamentary defence committees.
